findings.text: c1. The inner acts toward the resurrection: 34 verses (A1). This is the largest group.: *Denied*, and the ground Jesus gives: "the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit" (Act 23:8); Jesus' answer: "You are wrong, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God"; (Mat 22:29; Mar 12:24). He grounds it in God's name: "the God of Abraham" (Mar 12:26), "for; all live to him" (Luk 20:38); The section cites only Mat 22:30 and Luk 20:36, on marriage.; *Questioned, and not understood until later:*; "questioning what this rising from the dead might mean" (Mar 9:10); "as yet they did not understand the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead" (Joh 20:9); "When therefore he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this,; and they believed" (Joh 2:22); "Then he opened their minds to understand the Scriptures" (Luk 24:45–46); "Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead" (2Ti 2:8); *Known and believed:*; Martha: "I know that he will rise again in the resurrection on the last day" (Joh 11:24); then "Do you believe this?" "Yes, Lord; I believe" (11:26–27); *Mocked, deferred, thought incredible:*; "some mocked. But others said, 'We will hear you again about this'" (Act 17:32); "Why is it thought incredible by any of you that God raises the dead?" (Act 26:8); "the hope and the resurrection of the dead" on trial (Act 23:6; 24:21); *Faith emptied if it is not so:*; "how can some of you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?" (1Co 15:12); "your faith is futile and you are still in your sins" (15:17); "If in Christ we have hope in this life only, we are of all people most to be pitied" (15:19,; cited in *Life weighed*); The section cites none of 1Co 15:12–19. Faith (M13, OT-05.19) is a handle here.; *Upset:* "saying that the resurrection has already happened. They are upsetting the faith of; some" (2Ti 2:18).; *Feared, and a conscience stirred:*; the guards "lest his disciples … tell the people, 'He has risen from the dead'" (Mat 27:64); Herod: "John, whom I beheaded, has been raised" (Mar 6:16); "he was perplexed" (Luk 9:7); "that is why these miraculous powers are at work in him" (Mat 14:2); I read Herod's word as his own guilt speaking, since it names the beheading. The verses do not; say "guilt".
